clue.text: Fulfil Scottish takeaway order

blocks.note: first meaning: to complete or perform a task
second meaning: in Scotland, food or drink bought to take away

explanation.surface: Someone completes an order for food at a Scottish takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a carry-out is takeaway food or drink, so the surface order is itself the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry out a plan is to complete it; north of the border the same phrase names food bought to eat elsewhere.

clue.text: Zane Grey - occasionally visionary

indicators.note: something done only occasionally happens every so often, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the name

explanation.surface: The Western novelist Zane Grey is praised as a sometime visionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Aery is a variant spelling of airy, meaning ethereal or lofty in imagination, like a dreamy visionary idea.

clue.text: Rich intellect Lawrence possessed

indicators.note: what is possessed is held inside, so one piece is kept within the other

blocks.note: the initials of T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: A wealthy man of letters is said to have the intellect of Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia signed himself by his initials, a common crossword source for these two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Minted is British slang for very wealthy, as if one could print money of one's own.

clue.text: Issue heading off incitement against the state

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: the crime of stirring rebellion against the authorities

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline warns readers off a call to rebel against government.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S of SEDITION to leave EDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a newspaper or magazine is one edition of it, published at a given time.

clue.text: Family servant fee paid in advance

blocks.note: first meaning: a long-serving domestic employee of a household
second meaning: money paid up front to secure someone's services, as with a lawyer

explanation.surface: A household servant is paid wages before working.
explanation.definitionFit: An old retainer is a faithful household servant, and a lawyer's retainer is the sum paid beforehand to engage them.

clue.text: Exotic robes put on VP in religious ritual

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A vice president dons colourful foreign vestments for a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' means the rearranged robes are placed before the vice president's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An observance is a rite or ceremony kept as part of religious practice, such as a feast day.

clue.text: Spooner's enemy close? Not likely!

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words here exchange their starts

blocks.note: an enemy is a foe and close means near; swap the opening sounds of the pair

explanation.surface: A frightened reaction: an enemy close by? Surely not!
explanation.walkthrough: FOE NEAR with its first sounds swapped becomes NO FEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: No fear is a British colloquial exclamation of refusal, meaning there is no chance of that happening.

clue.text: An exceptional person, bloody Dicky!

blocks.note: a steak cooked bloody is served rare
a dicky bird is nursery talk for a little bird

explanation.surface: Someone praises a remarkable person while swearing at a man named Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a British swear word, but it describes undercooked meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare bird is an idiom for someone unusual, uncommon or exceptional among people.

clue.text: As one group, trash noble Conservative

indicators.note: to trash something is to wreck it, leaving the letters in a mess

explanation.surface: A crowd acting together attacks a Tory aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc is a French phrase used in English for all together, as a single unit.

clue.text: Sorry guys! Regulars only - it's a wild party

indicators.note: regular letters are those at even intervals, so only every second one is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: An apology: the bash is for regular guests only, and it's a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a riotous gathering marked by unrestrained revelry and indulgence.

clue.text: Streetcar runs into rock that measures four feet

indicators.note: a vehicle that runs into something ends up inside it here

blocks.note: American streetcar is a British tram

explanation.surface: A streetcar crashes into a boulder about four feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet' are the metrical units of verse, not body parts or a length, and 'rock' is a verb, not a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrameter is a line of verse made of four metrical units, so the line measures out four stresses.

clue.text: Supermodel commercial that's known for its intelligence

explanation.surface: A fashion advert praises its model for being clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on intelligence as cleverness; here it means espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: Mossad is Israel's national spy agency, famous for gathering secret information abroad.

clue.text: Ecstasy-fuelled rock band, endless energy, very imposing

indicators.note: something fuelled by a drug has it taken inside, so the drug sits within the band
without its end, the band's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Status Quo, the long-running British rock group

explanation.surface: A drug-addled rock group, out of steam, still cuts an impressive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: STATUS QUO loses its final O; E goes in after STATU, and a second E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque describes someone tall and dignified, like a statue, which is imposing in appearance.

clue.text: Unfussy diner ordering more vino

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer who isn't fussy asks for more wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plant and animal foods, so it is not picky about what is eaten.

clue.text: Retired TA soldier settled in Los Angeles, a city in the US

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so the letters are read backwards
someone settled in a place lives within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A former reservist soldier has made his home in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve, and a soldier is a kind of worker insect in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the state capital of Georgia, one of the largest cities in the American South.

clue.text: Enormous number hunt missing adult big cat

indicators.note: a thing missing from a word has been removed from it

blocks.note: to trail is to track or pursue
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A huge number of hunters fail to find a full-grown lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' reads as a noun, a party of hunters, but it is a verb meaning to follow a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A trillion is a million million, a vast figure used loosely for any huge quantity.

clue.text: Noble American maiden lady, rather old

blocks.note: M for maiden, a scoreless over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A dignified elderly American spinster is described.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored, recorded as M.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandam is an archaic word for grandmother or an old woman, hence a lady of advanced years.

clue.text: A measure of speed I built initially on northbound A1 (frog and toad?)

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: the A1 road, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A driver clocks a speed on the A1, Britain's Great North Road, heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: frogs and toads are members of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibia is the zoological class of cold-blooded vertebrates such as frogs, toads and newts that live on land and in water.

clue.text: Dreaded police stooges tap our houses

indicators.note: the words before it house the letters, holding them within

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Informers bug the phones in our homes for a feared secret force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' looks like a plural noun, but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany, notorious and widely feared.

clue.text: Use Mister Newton for spreading EU's bile

indicators.note: spreading things about scatters them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A call for a man called Newton to vent anti-European venom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like the title Mr, but it is a device that makes a mist.
explanation.definitionFit: To nebulise is to turn liquid into a fine spray, which is exactly what a mist sprayer does.

clue.text: Selfishness, for example, over one's millions?

blocks.note: O for over in cricket scoring
I for one, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A rich person hoarding their millions is held up as an example of greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is putting one's own interests first, the ethical stance of being self-centred.

clue.text: Klopp elated about taking on City

indicators.note: the words take on the letters, holding them within
turned about means facing back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Jürgen Klopp, the football manager, is thrilled about taking on Manchester City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a football team, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is an ancient city in northern Syria, among the oldest continuously inhabited places.

clue.text: Reply first of all right, receiving four points

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
something receiving others takes them inside

blocks.note: the four points of the compass

explanation.surface: A reply that is correct from the start earns four points in a quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R stand side by side, and NSWE goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a response to a question or message, the same as a reply.

clue.text: Direct last UNESCO missions

indicators.note: to direct is to arrange or manage, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer UNESCO's final assignments abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Consulates are diplomatic offices abroad, and a mission is another name for such a posting.

clue.text: Island cycling feature

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves letters from the front to the back

blocks.note: a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A feature of an island is that people ride bicycles there.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is used in Scottish place names for an islet; move its first two letters to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is part of the face, and facial parts are called features.

clue.text: Treat for starters consumed hot or cold

indicators.note: starters are the opening courses, so each word gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dish for the first course that can be eaten warm or chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc is an informal British word for a chocolate, a sweet indulgence or small reward.

clue.text: Old money key upper-class party

blocks.note: the escape key on a keyboard
U is the label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Old wealth is the passport to a posh party.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Before Tori Amos spends months in the capital

indicators.note: what is spent is used up and gone, so those letters are taken away

explanation.surface: Before her tour, singer Tori Amos spends months living in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: AMOS spends, or loses, MOS, leaving A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the executive seat of government of South Africa, one of its three capital cities.
